newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay stocks rally to end higher, short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Bombay stocks rally to end higher, short-covering.

text.p: ** (1030 GMT) - Pivotal stocks close higher, late rally
** Short-covering by speculators pushes prices up at close
** Last day of trade settlement at Bombay Stock Exchange
** Foreign funds buyers in select blue-chips, dealers say
** Bombay share index up 27.85 pts to 3,138.08, National
bourse index 3.94 pts to 892.94, both provisional
** ITC ends with sharp price changes at Bombay bourses
Bombay shares ended with small gains on Friday after a late rally driven by short-covering snapped an early dull price movement, dealers said.
The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) rose 27.85 points, or 0.90 percent, to close at a provisional 3,138.08, off 3,142.31, the intra-day high.
"There were some fireworks just before the session's close....lot of buying," said dealer Zubin Tampal at brokers Motilal Oswal.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index gained 3.94 points, or 0.44 percent, to close at 892.94 provisional.
Foreign funds were buyers in TISCO, BSES, Gujarat Ambuja, Larsen & Toubro, TELCO, Hindalco and BPCL, traders said.
The CRISIL 500-share index was up 2.77 points at a provisional close of 599.80.
Dealers said short-covering in pivotals on the last day of the weekly trade account at the BSE pushed share prices higher.
Speculators rushed to cover short-positions in shares of ITC which closed with sharp price differences at the Bombay bourses.
The stock advanced 8.25 rupees or 3.1 percent to end at 271.75 at the BSE with more than 1.64 million shares traded.
ITC climbed 2.0 rupees to 264.0 at the NSE.

Major shareholders of the troubled tobacco giant which include Indian financial institutions were meeting senior officials of its parent company, B.A.T. in Calcutta later on Friday to review operations of the company.
India's biggest cigarette company is alleged to have violated foreign exchange rules involving over $100 million, according to official sources.
SBI added 2.50 rupees to 222.25 rupees, L&T 6.25 to 225.50, TISCO 0.25 to 167.0, Reliance 3.25 to 187.75, TELCO 4.50 to 410.0, BSES 5.25 to 205.26 and ACC 27.0 to 1,390.0.
-- ANSHUMAN DAGA, Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
